# Archive entry name used as an extraction path (Go)

`qualor:go/zip-slip` · Issue · Severity: High · [CWE-22](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/22.html) · OWASP Top 10: [A01:2025 Broken Access Control](https://top10.owasp.org/2025/A01_2025-Broken_Access_Control/), [A01:2021 Broken Access Control](https://top10.owasp.org/2021/A01_2021-Broken_Access_Control/)

## What it finds

<!-- begin: what-it-finds -->
Archive extraction that uses the name of an entry, as stored in the archive, to build the path of
a file or directory it creates: the `Name` of an `archive/zip` file or of an `archive/tar` header,
reaching `os.Create`, `os.OpenFile`, `os.WriteFile`, `os.MkdirAll`, `os.Symlink` and similar calls.
<!-- end: what-it-finds -->

## Why it matters

<!-- begin: why-it-matters -->
The archive decides the entry names, and Go's readers accept names such as `../../etc/cron.d/x` or
`/home/app/.ssh/authorized_keys` unless `GODEBUG` says otherwise. Joining such a name to the
extraction directory writes outside it ("zip slip"): an uploaded archive can overwrite
configuration, code or keys and so take over the server.
<!-- end: why-it-matters -->

## Example

<!-- begin: example -->
**Noncompliant:** each entry is written to `dst` joined with its name.

```go
package unpack

import (
	"archive/zip"
	"io"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
)

func Unzip(src, dst string) error {
	r, err := zip.OpenReader(src)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	defer r.Close()
	for _, f := range r.File {
		out, err := os.Create(filepath.Join(dst, f.Name))
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		rc, _ := f.Open()
		io.Copy(out, rc)
		rc.Close()
		out.Close()
	}
	return nil
}
```

**Compliant:** entries whose name is not a local path are skipped.

```go
package unpack

import (
	"archive/zip"
	"io"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
)

func Unzip(src, dst string) error {
	r, err := zip.OpenReader(src)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	defer r.Close()
	for _, f := range r.File {
		if !filepath.IsLocal(f.Name) {
			continue
		}
		out, err := os.Create(filepath.Join(dst, f.Name))
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		rc, _ := f.Open()
		io.Copy(out, rc)
		rc.Close()
		out.Close()
	}
	return nil
}
```
<!-- end: example -->

## How to fix

<!-- begin: how-to-fix -->
- Create the files through an `os.Root` opened on the extraction directory (`os.OpenRoot(dst)`,
  then `root.Create(name)`), available since Go 1.24. It refuses names that leave the directory.
- Or skip (or reject) every entry whose name fails `filepath.IsLocal`.
- Treat link entries with the same care: a symbolic link inside the archive can point outside the
  directory.
<!-- end: how-to-fix -->

## Frameworks and APIs covered

- `archive/zip`
- `archive/tar`
- `os`

## Known limits

<!-- begin: known-limits -->
- A prefix check on the joined path (`strings.HasPrefix(target, dst+sep)`) and ad hoc checks such
  as `strings.Contains(name, "..")` are not recognised, so such code is still reported.
- `path.Base` and `filepath.Clean("/" + name)` do not count as making the name safe.
- An `IsLocal` check is recognised only as a simple guard (`if !filepath.IsLocal(n) { continue }`
  with a short body); one combined with other conditions, written in the `if`'s init statement, or
  in the true branch of an `if` with an `else`, is not, so the code is still reported.
- The guard must end by leaving: `return`, `continue` or `break` (also with a label), `panic`,
  `os.Exit`, or `log.Fatal`/`log.Panic` and their `f`/`ln` forms. The same methods of a
  `*log.Logger` count only when the logger's type is visible in the file (a parameter or a field);
  one taken from `log.Default()` is still reported. The rule reads the exit by its name, so a
  deferred `os.Exit`, or a `Fatal` method of another value called `log`, is taken as an exit.
- A program built with `GODEBUG=zipinsecurepath=0` (where the reader rejects such names) is still
  reported.
- `os.Chmod`, `os.Chtimes`, `os.Chown` and `os.Lchown` on the entry's path are not checked.
<!-- end: known-limits -->

## Tests

The test file [`rules/go/archive/zip-slip.go`](../../../rules/go/archive/zip-slip.go) holds every case the rule reports or accepts:
lines marked `ruleid:` must be reported and lines marked `ok:` must not. The known limits are
marked `todoruleid:` (missed) and `todook:` (wrongly reported). `npm test` runs them with OpenGrep,
and checks the example above as well.

The rule: [`rules/go/archive/zip-slip.yml`](../../../rules/go/archive/zip-slip.yml), added in version 2026.10.1.
